register: OBSERVED COUNTS from a DRY decision-path run, stub bridge, no engine. Counts of decisions and beliefs, never of seconds.

card_ruling.verdict: NO PROACTIVE MECHANISM ON THE CARD
claims_quoted: we developed a prediction-based early rejection policy
its architecture maximises KVCache reuse across a disaggregated prefill/decode pool
maximise KVCache reuse -> serve GPU-warm, then host-warm, then cold (MOONCAKE-REUSE-FIRST order) | FAITHFUL in effect
card_ruling.not_reproduced_quoted: The disaggregated architecture; the transfer engine and its storage tiers; the TBT SLO; the paper's throughput results.
card_ruling.reasoning: Both quoted mechanisms are triggered BY a request. Neither creates cache for a request that has not arrived. The transfer engine, which is where any prefetch would live, is explicitly NOT REPRODUCED. Giving mooncake a warm-ahead lever would hand it a capability its card does not claim.
card_ruling.revises: reports/policy_v5_assessment.md section I, which recorded 'probably yes, needs a ruling' on the grounds that cache-centric scheduling is 'the closest published analogue to warm-ahead'. An analogy is not a claim.

step2_verdict.causal_link: KVCache reuse -> MOONCAKE-REUSE-FIRST order -> which recall is served first -> more reuse, lower TTFT, more on-time answers
step2_verdict.implementing_quantity: RecallQuery.readiness, the first sort key of MooncakeAdapted.decide
step2_verdict.classification: CONSTANT: the sort key takes one value in every epoch, so the reuse-first order is identical to deadline order and the mechanism cannot affect any decision. A CLAUDE.md Step 2 stopping condition.
step2_verdict.prior_channel_finding: cards/mooncake.md D130 port note: coordinator.py never reads Action.order, so the reuse-first order cannot reach a decision in live2 even when the signal varies. This audit adds the SIGNAL half.

no_arm_added: No mooncake arm is registered by this file. Its committed cells are unaffected and need no relabelling, because no proactive mechanism was withheld from it.
